item.title: On a small farm
item.description: Visit a small farm and learn words for the animals, places, and things you see there.

children.definition: A large female farm animal that gives milk and whose young are called calves.
children.example: We see a cow by the gate.

children.definition: A large animal that people can ride.
children.example: A horse is eating hay by the barn.

children.definition: A farm animal with a thick coat of wool.
children.example: We see a sheep in the field.

children.definition: A farm animal that often has horns and a small beard.
children.example: A goat stands on a rock near the fence.

children.definition: A farm animal with a flat nose and a short, curly tail.
children.example: A pig is asleep in the shade beside the barn.
We see a hen sitting on her eggs.

children.definition: An animal like a small horse with long ears.
children.example: A donkey stands beside the farm cart.

children.definition: A large farm building where people keep animals or hay.
children.example: The farmer keeps hay in the barn.
children.translation_uz: pichan saqlanadigan yoki mol boqiladigan katta xoʻjalik binosi

children.definition: A part of a fence that you open to go through.
children.example: Please shut the gate after you.

children.definition: A barrier around an area, for example to keep animals inside.
children.example: We look at the pigs through the fence.

children.definition: An open area of land for farm animals or plants.
children.example: The sheep are eating grass in the field.

children.definition: Grass that people cut and dry for animals to eat.
children.example: The farmer gives hay to the donkey.

children.definition: The soft hair that grows on a sheep.
children.example: We touch some wool from the farm's sheep.

children.definition: A farm vehicle with big wheels that can pull heavy things.
children.example: The farmer drives a tractor across the field.
